title: Shepherd's Pie
subtitle: Braised lamb mince under a creamy mashed potato crust
excerpt: Ground lamb braised with onion, carrot, and stock, finished with a thick layer of smooth mashed potato and baked until golden. A British comfort dish that's one of the most satisfying things to eat on a cold evening.

recipe.sourceNotes: Shepherd's pie is a British dish that takes its name from the lamb it contains: shepherds tend sheep. The distinction between shepherd's pie (lamb) and cottage pie (beef) is firm; using beef and calling it shepherd's pie is widely considered incorrect. The dish emerged in the late nineteenth century as a way of using leftover roast meat, layered under mashed potato and baked again. Modern versions use raw mince rather than leftovers, which gives a more uniform texture. The mashed potato crust should be smooth and creamy enough to pipe or spread, thick enough not to sink into the filling, and baked long enough to develop a pale golden crust with brown patches. Worcestershire sauce in the filling is standard and adds depth.

content.text: Reduce the lamb filling until it is thick and the liquid has almost gone before adding the potato; a wet filling makes the potato topping sink and go grey. The potato must be very well seasoned and have enough butter and milk to spread smoothly without cracking.

items.preparation: use lamb mince for the traditional shepherd's pie
floury variety such as Maris Piper; peeled and quartered

content.text: Heat the oil in a large, deep pan. Cook the onion and carrot over medium heat for 8 minutes until soft. Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute. Increase the heat, add the mince, and break it up well. Cook until browned all over.

Add the tomato puree. Cook for 2 minutes. Add the Worcestershire sauce, stock, thyme, and bay leaves. Season. Bring to a simmer and cook for 25 to 30 minutes until the liquid has reduced to a thick, glossy gravy. Discard the bay leaves. Taste and adjust salt.
While the filling cooks, boil the potatoes in well-salted water for 20 minutes until very tender. Drain thoroughly. Mash with the butter and warm milk until very smooth. Season generously.

Heat the oven to 200°C / fan 180°C / gas 6. Transfer the filling to a large baking dish. Spoon the mashed potato over and spread it evenly, then rough up the surface with a fork. Bake for 20 to 25 minutes until the potato is golden and the filling is bubbling at the edges.
